A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 13-page PartDiffuser paper, including references and Appendices A–C. Text comparison and page rendering establish that the content matches apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original mesh-generation experiments, conditioning ablations and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–3, plus segmentation robustness results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark, ablation, efficiency and appendix robustness results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical segmentation, tokenization, hierarchical conditioning, diffusion objectives, attention masks and part-wise sampling procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Objaverse and 3DFront and evaluate point-cloud-to-mesh generation on Objaverse, HSSD and 3DFront. Appendix test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 3 compare against the same MeshAnythingV2, BPT and TreeMeshGPT baselines. No comparator is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 and Appendices A–B retain the same splits, preprocessing, training budgets, model configuration and evaluation procedures, including 300 test samples per dataset and CD, HD, EMD and F1 metrics.

E4.justification: The conditioning ablations, sampling-acceleration analysis, SAMPart3D segmentation robustness experiment and sampling-process case studies are identical in Tables 2–3 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match, including Tables 1–3 and Appendix C. For example, PartDiffuser's Objaverse CD×1000 remains 17.813 and F1 remains 0.343.

T1.justification: The attention equations, likelihood factorization and diffusion objective in Section 3.3, together with the segmentation bounds in Appendix A, are identical. No formal results or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain identical claims about balancing global structure and local detail through part-wise diffusion and improving mesh reconstruction quality.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged, including Appendix C. Section 5.1 retains the same limitations concerning model capacity, context length, sampling efficiency and upstream segmentation.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–B provide identical implementation information, including H100 hardware, training durations, data filtering, token limits, attention masks and noise schedules.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research positioning throughout the paper and all 46 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 26 Mar 2026 to v3 dated 16 May 2026, with its version link updated accordingly. This is an administrative text edit; prose, terminology and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–3, Algorithm 1, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–13 are pixel-identical; first-page visual differences are confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 retains the same scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations, including all appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and corresponding self-link produces no meaningful change in paper quality.
